# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Readings in a time range

`table.between(from, to)` returns the readings with `from <= minute <= to` in order; invalid or reversed ranges raise `ArgumentError`.

## Chart datum offset

`Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)`: `add` stores the gauge height plus the datum, so all reported heights are chart heights. `table.datum_cm` returns the offset.

## Height at any minute

`table.height_at(minute)` interpolates linearly between neighbouring readings and rounds half up; outside the readings it raises `Tidelog::OutOfRange`.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:peak` / `:trough`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## CSV export and import

`table.to_csv` writes `minute;height_cm` and a line per reading; `Tidelog::Table.from_csv(port, text)` reads it back (blank lines skipped, errors name the `line N`).

## High-water alarms

`table.alarm(threshold_cm) { |reading| ... }` calls the block (after the reading is stored) for every `add` at or above the threshold, in registration order. A raising block propagates but the reading stays.

## Navigable windows

`table.windows(min_cm)` returns `Tidelog::Window`s (`from`, `to`, `minutes`, `cover?`, `to_s`): the maximal runs of whole minutes in which the interpolated height is at least `min_cm`.

## Merging tables

`table.merge(other, on_conflict: :error)` adds the other table's readings and returns a `Tidelog::MergeReport` (`added`, `conflicts`). Equal readings are ignored; for differing heights `:error` raises, `:keep`, `:replace` and `:average` (half up) resolve them.

module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
      @alarms = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      @alarms.each { |limit, block| block.call(reading) if reading.height_cm >= limit }
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute;height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute};#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute;height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute;height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*;\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute;height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end

    def alarm(threshold_cm, &block)
      raise ArgumentError, "threshold must be an integer" unless threshold_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "a block is required" if block.nil?

      @alarms << [threshold_cm, block]
      nil
    end

    def windows(min_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "min_cm must be an integer" unless min_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      return [] if @readings.empty?

      found = []
      start = nil

        elsif start
          found << Window.new(start, m - 1)
          start = nil
        end
      end
      found << Window.new(start, @readings.last.minute) if start
      found
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }

      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]

          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"

        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Readings in a time range

`table.between(from, to)` returns the readings with `from <= minute <= to` in order; invalid or reversed ranges raise `ArgumentError`.

## Chart datum offset

`Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)`: `add` stores the gauge height plus the datum, so all reported heights are chart heights. `table.datum_cm` returns the offset.

## Height at any minute

`table.height_at(minute)` interpolates linearly between neighbouring readings and rounds half up; outside the readings it raises `Tidelog::OutOfRange`.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:peak` / `:trough`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## High-water alarms

`table.alarm(threshold_cm) { |reading| ... }` calls the block (after the reading is stored) for every `add` at or above the threshold, in registration order. A raising block propagates but the reading stays.

## Navigable windows

`table.windows(min_cm)` returns `Tidelog::Window`s (`from`, `to`, `minutes`, `cover?`, `to_s`): the maximal runs of whole minutes in which the interpolated height is at least `min_cm`.

## Merging tables

`table.merge(other, on_conflict: :error)` adds the other table's readings and returns a `Tidelog::MergeReport` (`added`, `conflicts`). Equal readings are ignored; for differing heights `:error` raises, `:keep`, `:replace` and `:average` (half up) resolve them.

module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
      @alarms = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      @alarms.each { |limit, block| block.call(reading) if reading.height_cm >= limit }
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def alarm(threshold_cm, &block)
      raise ArgumentError, "threshold must be an integer" unless threshold_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "a block is required" if block.nil?

      @alarms << [threshold_cm, block]
      nil
    end

    def windows(min_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "min_cm must be an integer" unless min_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      return [] if @readings.empty?

      found = []
      start = nil
      (@readings.first.minute..@readings.last.minute).each do |m|
        if height_at(m) >= min_cm
          start ||= m
        elsif start
          found << Window.new(start, m - 1)
          start = nil
        end
      end
      found << Window.new(start, @readings.last.minute) if start
      found
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }
      added = []
      conflicts = []
      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]
        if own.nil?
          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"
      end

      added.each { |r| @readings << Reading.new(r.minute, r.height_cm) }
      conflicts.each do |own, theirs|
        case on_conflict
        when :replace then own.set_height(theirs.height_cm)
        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

module Tidelog
  # A stretch of whole minutes, both ends included.
  Window = Struct.new(:from, :to) do
    def minutes
      to - from + 1
    end

    def cover?(minute)
      minute >= from && minute <= to
    end

    def to_s
      "#{Tidelog.label(from)}-#{Tidelog.label(to)}"
    end
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"
require "tidelog"

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class BasicTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @t = Tidelog::Table.new("Port Marrow")
  end

  def fill(table = @t, data = DATA)
    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_add_and_order
    fill(@t, DATA.reverse)
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
    assert_equal [0, 180, 360, 540, 720], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal 340, @t.highest.height_cm
    assert_equal 60, @t.lowest.height_cm
    assert_raises(Tidelog::DuplicateReading) { @t.add(180, 1) }
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
  end

  def test_validation
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(-1, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(1.5, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(5, "10") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("  ") }
    assert_equal 0, @t.count
  end

  def test_report
    @t.add(75, 312)
    @t.add(1515, -8)
    assert_equal "D0 01:15 312 cm\nD1 01:15 -8 cm\n", @t.report
    assert_equal "D1 01:15", Tidelog.label(1515)
  end
  def test_mean_basic
    fill
    assert_equal 184, @t.mean_height
    assert_equal 280, @t.tidal_range
  end

  def test_between_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [180, 360], @t.between(100, 400).map(&:minute)
  end

  def test_datum_basic
    t = Tidelog::Table.new("Quay", datum_cm: 20)
    assert_equal 120, t.add(0, 100).height_cm
  end

  def test_height_at_basic
    fill
    assert_equal 230, @t.height_at(90)
    assert_equal 340, @t.height_at(180)
  end

  def test_correct_basic
    fill
    assert_equal 350, @t.correct(180, 10).height_cm
  end

  def test_turning_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [:peak, :trough, :peak], @t.turning_points.map(&:first)
  end

  def test_alarm_basic
    seen = []
    @t.alarm(300) { |r| seen << r.minute }
    fill
    assert_equal [180, 540], seen
  end

  def test_windows_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [[66, 281], [450, 619]], @t.windows(200).map { |w| [w.from, w.to] }
  end

  def test_merge_basic
    a = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("A"), [[0, 1]])
    b = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("B"), [[10, 2]])
    assert_equal 1, a.merge(b).added
    assert_equal 2, a.count
  end
end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Chart datum offset

`Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)`: `add` stores the gauge height plus the datum, so all reported heights are chart heights. `table.datum_cm` returns the offset.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## Merging tables

`table.merge(other, on_conflict: :error)` adds the other table's readings and returns a `Tidelog::MergeReport` (`added`, `conflicts`). Equal readings are ignored; for differing heights `:error` raises, `:keep`, `:replace` and `:average` (half up) resolve them.
solution.lib/tidelog/table.rb:
module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }
      added = []
      conflicts = []
      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]
        if own.nil?
          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"
      end

      added.each { |r| @readings << Reading.new(r.minute, r.height_cm) }
      conflicts.each do |own, theirs|
        case on_conflict
        when :replace then own.set_height(theirs.height_cm)
        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

# Design note: Gauge corrections
Status: approved | Owner: Priya

### Motivation
Readings need to be corrected after the fact, with a trail.

### Behaviour
1. `table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adds `delta_cm` to the height of the reading at exactly that minute and returns the reading. `delta_cm` must be a non-zero integer (`ArgumentError`, checked first); a minute without a reading raises `KeyError`.
2. `table.corrections` returns a new array of `[minute, delta_cm]` pairs, one per successful correction, in the order they were made.

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does.

  # One measured water height.
  class Reading
    attr_reader :minute, :height_cm

    def initialize(minute, height_cm)
      @minute = minute
      @height_cm = height_cm
    end

    def to_s
      "#{Tidelog.label(minute)} #{height_cm} cm"

    # Used by the table; not meant to be called from outside.
    def set_height(height)
      @height_cm = height
    end
  end

require "minitest/autorun"
require "tidelog"

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class BasicTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @t = Tidelog::Table.new("Port Marrow")
  end

  def fill(table = @t, data = DATA)
    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_add_and_order
    fill(@t, DATA.reverse)
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
    assert_equal [0, 180, 360, 540, 720], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal 340, @t.highest.height_cm
    assert_equal 60, @t.lowest.height_cm
    assert_raises(Tidelog::DuplicateReading) { @t.add(180, 1) }
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
  end

  def test_validation
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(-1, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(1.5, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(5, "10") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("  ") }
    assert_equal 0, @t.count
  end

    @t.add(75, 312)
    @t.add(1515, -8)

  end

    assert_equal 280, @t.tidal_range
  end

    assert_equal 120, t.add(0, 100).height_cm
  end

  def test_merge_basic
    a = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("A"), [[0, 1]])
    b = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("B"), [[10, 2]])
    assert_equal 1, a.merge(b).added
    assert_equal 2, a.count
  end
end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Readings in a time range

`table.between(from, to)` returns the readings with `from <= minute <= to` in order; invalid or reversed ranges raise `ArgumentError`.

## Chart datum offset

`Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)`: `add` stores the gauge height plus the datum, so all reported heights are chart heights. `table.datum_cm` returns the offset.

## Height at any minute

`table.height_at(minute)` interpolates linearly between neighbouring readings and rounds half up; outside the readings it raises `Tidelog::OutOfRange`.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:peak` / `:trough`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## CSV export and import

`table.to_csv` writes `minute,height_cm` and a line per reading; `Tidelog::Table.from_csv(port, text)` reads it back (blank lines skipped, errors name the `line N`).

## Navigable windows

`table.windows(min_cm)` returns `Tidelog::Window`s (`from`, `to`, `minutes`, `cover?`, `to_s`): the maximal runs of whole minutes in which the interpolated height is at least `min_cm`.

module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute,height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute},#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute,height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute,height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute,height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end

    def windows(min_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "min_cm must be an integer" unless min_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      return [] if @readings.empty?

      found = []
      start = nil
      (@readings.first.minute..@readings.last.minute).each do |m|
        if height_at(m) >= min_cm
          start ||= m
        elsif start
          found << Window.new(start, m - 1)
          start = nil
        end
      end
      found << Window.new(start, @readings.last.minute) if start
      found
    end
  end
end

      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute,height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute},#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute,height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute,height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute,height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end

    def windows(min_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "min_cm must be an integer" unless min_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      return [] if @readings.empty?

      found = []
      start = nil
      (@readings.first.minute..@readings.last.minute).each do |m|
        if height_at(m) >= min_cm
          start ||= m
        elsif start
          found << Window.new(start, m - 1)
          start = nil
        end
      end
      found << Window.new(start, @readings.last.minute) if start
      found
    end
  end
end

module Tidelog
  # A stretch of whole minutes, both ends included.
  Window = Struct.new(:from, :to) do
    def minutes
      to - from + 1
    end

    def cover?(minute)
      minute >= from && minute <= to
    end

    def to_s
      "#{Tidelog.label(from)}-#{Tidelog.label(to)}"
    end
  end
end

# Design note: Chart datum offset and Gauge corrections
Status: approved | Owner: Tomasz

## Chart datum offset
Motivation:
The gauge at the quay was re-levelled and its zero no longer matches the chart datum.

Behaviour:
1. `Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)` takes an integer option `datum_cm` (default 0; anything else is an `ArgumentError`) and `table.datum_cm` returns it. `add` takes the raw gauge height and stores gauge height plus datum; every height the table reports (`Reading#height_cm`, `highest`, `report`, ...) is that chart height.
2. `to_csv` writes the heights as `readings` reports them (chart heights, datum included); `Table.from_csv` always builds a table without a datum, so the numbers in the file are taken as they are.

## Gauge corrections
Motivation:
The gauge reader fat-fingered a reading last week and the table has been wrong ever since.

Behaviour:
1. `table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adds `delta_cm` to the height of the reading at exactly that minute and returns the reading. `delta_cm` must be a non-zero integer (`ArgumentError`, checked first); a minute without a reading raises `KeyError`.
2. `table.corrections` returns a new array of `[minute, delta_cm]` pairs, one per successful correction, in the order they were made.

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does. Match the style of the surrounding code.

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
      @alarms = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      @alarms.each { |limit, block| block.call(reading) if reading.height_cm >= limit }
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute;height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute};#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute;height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute;height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*;\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute;height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end

    def alarm(threshold_cm, &block)
      raise ArgumentError, "threshold must be an integer" unless threshold_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "a block is required" if block.nil?

      @alarms << [threshold_cm, block]
      nil
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }
      added = []
      conflicts = []
      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]
        if own.nil?
          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"
      end

      added.each { |r| @readings << Reading.new(r.minute, r.height_cm) }
      conflicts.each do |own, theirs|
        case on_conflict
        when :replace then own.set_height(theirs.height_cm)
        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).

  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.

require "minitest/autorun"
require "tidelog"

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class BasicTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @t = Tidelog::Table.new("Port Marrow")
  end

  def fill(table = @t, data = DATA)
    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_add_and_order
    fill(@t, DATA.reverse)
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
    assert_equal [0, 180, 360, 540, 720], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal 340, @t.highest.height_cm
    assert_equal 60, @t.lowest.height_cm
    assert_raises(Tidelog::DuplicateReading) { @t.add(180, 1) }
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
  end

  def test_validation
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(-1, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(1.5, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(5, "10") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("  ") }
    assert_equal 0, @t.count
  end

  def test_report
    @t.add(75, 312)
    @t.add(1515, -8)
    assert_equal "D0 01:15 312 cm\nD1 01:15 -8 cm\n", @t.report
    assert_equal "D1 01:15", Tidelog.label(1515)
  end
  def test_between_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [180, 360], @t.between(100, 400).map(&:minute)
  end

  def test_datum_basic
    t = Tidelog::Table.new("Quay", datum_cm: 20)
    assert_equal 120, t.add(0, 100).height_cm
  end

  def test_correct_basic
    fill
    assert_equal 350, @t.correct(180, 10).height_cm
  end

  def test_turning_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [:peak, :trough, :peak], @t.turning_points.map(&:first)
  end

  def test_csv_basic
    fill
    assert_equal "minute;height_cm\n0;120\n", @t.to_csv.lines.first(2).join
  end

  def test_alarm_basic
    seen = []
    @t.alarm(300) { |r| seen << r.minute }
    fill
    assert_equal [180, 540], seen
  end

  def test_merge_basic
    a = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("A"), [[0, 1]])
    b = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("B"), [[10, 2]])
    assert_equal 1, a.merge(b).added
    assert_equal 2, a.count
  end
end

require "tidelog"

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class FeatureTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @t = Tidelog::Table.new("Port Marrow")
  end

  def fill(table = @t, data = DATA)
    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_base_rules
    assert_equal "Harbour", Tidelog::Table.new("  Harbour ").port
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new(nil) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("Harbour", colour: "blue") }
    r = @t.add(0, 100)
    assert_equal [0, 100], [r.minute, r.height_cm]
    @t.add(10, 100)
    assert_equal 0, @t.highest.minute
    assert_equal 0, @t.lowest.minute
    @t.add(5, 100)
    assert_equal 0, @t.highest.minute

      assert_raises(ArgumentError, [m, h].inspect) { @t.add(m, h) }
    end
    assert_raises(Tidelog::DuplicateReading) { @t.add(5, 7) }
    assert_equal [0, 5, 10], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal [100, 100, 100], @t.readings.map(&:height_cm)
    @t.readings.clear
    assert_equal 3, @t.count
    assert_kind_of Tidelog::Error, Tidelog::DuplicateReading.new
    empty = Tidelog::Table.new("Nowhere")
    assert_nil empty.highest
    assert_nil empty.lowest
    assert_equal "", empty.report
  end

    assert_equal "D0 23:59", Tidelog.label(1439)
    assert_equal "D2 10:07", Tidelog.label(2 * 1440 + 607)

    assert_equal "D0 00:59 0 cm", @t.readings.first.to_s

  end

    assert_equal [], fill(Tidelog::Table.new("Ramp"), [[0, 1], [5, 2], [9, 3]]).turning_points
  end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:high` / `:low`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## CSV export and import

`table.to_csv` writes `minute,height_cm` and a line per reading; `Tidelog::Table.from_csv(port, text)` reads it back (blank lines skipped, errors name the `line N`).

## Merging tables

`table.merge(other, on_conflict: :error)` adds the other table's readings and returns a `Tidelog::MergeReport` (`added`, `conflicts`). Equal readings are ignored; for differing heights `:error` raises, `:keep`, `:replace` and `:average` (half up) resolve them.
solution.lib/tidelog/table.rb:
module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:high, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:low, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute,height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute},#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute,height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute,height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute,height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }
      added = []
      conflicts = []
      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]
        if own.nil?
          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"
      end

      added.each { |r| @readings << Reading.new(r.minute, r.height_cm) }
      conflicts.each do |own, theirs|
        case on_conflict
        when :replace then own.set_height(theirs.height_cm)
        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class BasicTest < Minitest::Test

  end

    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_add_and_order

    assert_equal 5, @t.count
    assert_equal [0, 180, 360, 540, 720], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal 340, @t.highest.height_cm

  end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Height at any minute

`table.height_at(minute)` interpolates linearly between neighbouring readings and rounds half up; outside the readings it raises `Tidelog::OutOfRange`.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:peak` / `:trough`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## CSV export and import

`table.to_csv` writes `minute,height_cm` and a line per reading; `Tidelog::Table.from_csv(port, text)` reads it back (blank lines skipped, errors name the `line N`).
solution.lib/tidelog/table.rb:
module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def to_csv
      "minute,height_cm\n" + @readings.map { |r| "#{r.minute},#{r.height_cm}\n" }.join
    end

    def self.from_csv(port, text)
      lines = text.to_s.lines.map(&:chomp)
      unless lines.first.to_s.strip == "minute,height_cm"
        raise ArgumentError, "line 1: the header must be minute,height_cm"
      end

      table = new(port)
      lines.each_with_index do |line, i|
        next if i.zero? || line.strip.empty?

        m = line.match(/\A\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(-?\d+)\s*\z/)
        raise ArgumentError, "line #{i + 1}: expected minute,height" unless m

        begin
          table.add(m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i)
        rescue DuplicateReading => e
          raise DuplicateReading, "line #{i + 1}: #{e.message}"
        end
      end
      table
    end
  end
end

module Tidelog
  # "D1 01:15" for minute 1515.
  def self.label(minute)

  end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Readings in a time range

`table.between(from, to)` returns the readings with `from <= minute <= to` in order; invalid or reversed ranges raise `ArgumentError`.

## Chart datum offset

`Tidelog::Table.new(port, datum_cm: 0)`: `add` stores the gauge height plus the datum, so all reported heights are chart heights. `table.datum_cm` returns the offset.

## Height at any minute

`table.height_at(minute)` interpolates linearly between neighbouring readings and rounds half up; outside the readings it raises `Tidelog::OutOfRange`.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:high` / `:low`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.
solution.lib/tidelog/table.rb:
module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class OutOfRange < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      datum = opts.delete(:datum_cm) { 0 }
      raise ArgumentError, "datum_cm must be an integer" unless datum.is_a?(Integer)

      @datum_cm = datum
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      height_cm += @datum_cm
      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    attr_reader :datum_cm

    def height_at(minute)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      if @readings.empty? || minute < @readings.first.minute || minute > @readings.last.minute
        raise OutOfRange, "no readings around minute #{minute}"
      end

      lo = @readings.select { |r| r.minute <= minute }.last
      return lo.height_cm if lo.minute == minute

      hi = @readings.find { |r| r.minute > minute }
      exact = Rational(lo.height_cm * (hi.minute - minute) + hi.height_cm * (minute - lo.minute), hi.minute - lo.minute)
      (exact + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:high, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:low, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end
  end
end

module Tidelog
  # One measured water height.
  class Reading
    attr_reader :minute, :height_cm

    def initialize(minute, height_cm)
      @minute = minute
      @height_cm = height_cm
    end

    def to_s
      "#{Tidelog.label(minute)} #{height_cm} cm"
    end

    # Used by the table; not meant to be called from outside.
    def apply_delta(delta)
      @height_cm += delta
    end
  end
end

# tidelog

A tide table for a harbour office, as a small Ruby library (Ruby 3.3, standard library only). Run the tests with
`ruby -Ilib -Itest -e 'Dir["test/test_*.rb"].sort.each { |f| require "./#{f}" }'`.

## Layout

* `lib/tidelog.rb`: requires everything and has `Tidelog.label`.
* `lib/tidelog/reading.rb`: `Tidelog::Reading`.
* `lib/tidelog/table.rb`: `Tidelog::Table` and the errors.

## Basics

Time is a whole number of minutes counted from midnight of day 0 of the log; heights are whole centimetres (they may
be negative).

* `Tidelog::Table.new(port)`; the port name must not be blank and is stripped (`ArgumentError`), and `table.port` returns
  it. Unknown options raise `ArgumentError` (there are no options yet).
* `table.add(minute, height_cm)` stores a reading and returns the `Tidelog::Reading` (`minute`, `height_cm`). The minute
  must be a non-negative integer and the height an integer (`ArgumentError`); a second reading for the same minute
  raises `Tidelog::DuplicateReading`. A failed `add` changes nothing.
* `table.readings` is a new array of the readings ordered by minute, `table.count` their number. `table.highest` and
  `table.lowest` return the reading with the largest / smallest height (the earliest one on a tie) or `nil` when the
  table is empty.
* `Tidelog.label(minute)` formats a minute as `D<day> HH:MM` (`D1 01:15` for 1515). `reading.to_s` is
  `<label> <height> cm`, and `table.report` has one such line per reading, each ending in a newline.

## Mean height and range

`table.mean_height` is the mean height rounded half up (towards +infinity); `table.tidal_range` is highest minus
lowest. Both are `nil` for an empty table.

## Readings in a time range

`table.between(from, to)` returns the readings with `from <= minute <= to` in order; invalid or reversed ranges raise `ArgumentError`.

## Gauge corrections

`table.correct(minute, delta_cm)` adjusts one reading (non-zero integer delta; `KeyError` for a minute without a reading) and `table.corrections` lists the `[minute, delta]` pairs made so far.

## High and low water

`table.turning_points` returns `[kind, reading]` pairs (`:peak` / `:trough`); equal consecutive heights form one level, represented by its earliest reading, and the first and last level never count.

## Merging tables

`table.merge(other, on_conflict: :error)` adds the other table's readings and returns a `Tidelog::MergeReport` (`added`, `conflicts`). Equal readings are ignored; for differing heights `:error` raises, `:keep`, `:replace` and `:average` (half up) resolve them.
solution.lib/tidelog/table.rb:
module Tidelog
  class Error < StandardError; end

  class DuplicateReading < Error; end

  class Table
    attr_reader :port

    def initialize(port, **opts)
      raise ArgumentError, "port is required" if port.to_s.strip.empty?

      raise ArgumentError, "unknown option(s): #{opts.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.join(', ')}" unless opts.empty?

      @port = port.to_s.strip
      @readings = []
      @corrections = []
    end

    def add(minute, height_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "minute must be a non-negative integer" unless minute.is_a?(Integer) && minute >= 0
      raise ArgumentError, "height must be an integer" unless height_cm.is_a?(Integer)
      raise DuplicateReading, "there is already a reading at minute #{minute}" if @readings.any? { |r| r.minute == minute }

      reading = Reading.new(minute, height_cm)
      @readings << reading
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      reading
    end

    def readings
      @readings.dup
    end

    def count
      @readings.size
    end

    def highest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm > best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def lowest
      @readings.reduce(nil) { |best, r| best.nil? || r.height_cm < best.height_cm ? r : best }
    end

    def report
      @readings.map { |r| "#{r}\n" }.join
    end

    def mean_height
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      (Rational(@readings.sum(&:height_cm), @readings.size) + Rational(1, 2)).floor
    end

    def tidal_range
      return nil if @readings.empty?

      highest.height_cm - lowest.height_cm
    end

    def between(from, to)
      raise ArgumentError, "from and to must be integers" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && to.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "from must not be after to" if from > to

      @readings.select { |r| r.minute >= from && r.minute <= to }
    end

    def correct(minute, delta_cm)
      raise ArgumentError, "delta must be a non-zero integer" unless delta_cm.is_a?(Integer) && !delta_cm.zero?

      reading = @readings.find { |r| r.minute == minute }
      raise KeyError, "no reading at minute #{minute}" if reading.nil?

      reading.apply_delta(delta_cm)
      @corrections << [minute, delta_cm]
      reading
    end

    def corrections
      @corrections.map(&:dup)
    end

    def turning_points
      levels = []
      @readings.each do |r|
        if levels.last && levels.last.height_cm == r.height_cm
          next
        end
        levels << r
      end
      found = []
      (1...(levels.size - 1)).each do |i|
        before = levels[i - 1].height_cm
        here = levels[i].height_cm
        after = levels[i + 1].height_cm
        if here > before && here > after
          found << [:peak, levels[i]]
        elsif here < before && here < after
          found << [:trough, levels[i]]
        end
      end
      found
    end

    def merge(other, on_conflict: :error)
      raise ArgumentError, "other must be a Tidelog::Table" unless other.is_a?(Table)
      raise ArgumentError, "unknown policy: #{on_conflict.inspect}" unless %i[error keep replace average].include?(on_conflict)

      mine = @readings.to_h { |r| [r.minute, r] }
      added = []
      conflicts = []
      other.readings.each do |r|
        own = mine[r.minute]
        if own.nil?
          added << r
        elsif own.height_cm != r.height_cm
          conflicts << [own, r]
        end
      end
      if on_conflict == :error && !conflicts.empty?
        raise DuplicateReading, "the tables disagree at minute #{conflicts.first[0].minute}"
      end

      added.each { |r| @readings << Reading.new(r.minute, r.height_cm) }
      conflicts.each do |own, theirs|
        case on_conflict
        when :replace then own.set_height(theirs.height_cm)
        when :average then own.set_height((Rational(own.height_cm + theirs.height_cm, 2) + Rational(1, 2)).floor)
        end
      end
      @readings.sort_by!(&:minute)
      MergeReport.new(added.size, conflicts.map { |own, _| own.minute })
    end
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"
require "tidelog"

# A day and a half of a semi-diurnal tide: high at 03:00 and 09:00, low at 06:00, falling to the end.
DATA = [[0, 120], [180, 340], [360, 90], [540, 310], [720, 60]].freeze unless defined?(DATA)

class BasicTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    @t = Tidelog::Table.new("Port Marrow")
  end

  def fill(table = @t, data = DATA)
    data.each { |m, h| table.add(m, h) }
    table
  end

  def test_add_and_order
    fill(@t, DATA.reverse)
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
    assert_equal [0, 180, 360, 540, 720], @t.readings.map(&:minute)
    assert_equal 340, @t.highest.height_cm
    assert_equal 60, @t.lowest.height_cm
    assert_raises(Tidelog::DuplicateReading) { @t.add(180, 1) }
    assert_equal 5, @t.count
  end

  def test_validation
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(-1, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(1.5, 10) }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { @t.add(5, "10") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Tidelog::Table.new("  ") }
    assert_equal 0, @t.count
  end

  def test_report
    @t.add(75, 312)
    @t.add(1515, -8)
    assert_equal "D0 01:15 312 cm\nD1 01:15 -8 cm\n", @t.report
    assert_equal "D1 01:15", Tidelog.label(1515)
  end
  def test_mean_basic
    fill
    assert_equal 184, @t.mean_height
    assert_equal 280, @t.tidal_range
  end

  def test_between_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [180, 360], @t.between(100, 400).map(&:minute)
  end

  def test_turning_basic
    fill
    assert_equal [:peak, :trough, :peak], @t.turning_points.map(&:first)
  end

  def test_merge_basic
    a = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("A"), [[0, 1]])
    b = fill(Tidelog::Table.new("B"), [[10, 2]])
    assert_equal 1, a.merge(b).added
    assert_equal 2, a.count
  end
end

  end

    a, b = merge_pair
